name: Noah
title: Righteous man and builder of the ark
summary: Noah was a righteous man who lived in a time when the world was full of evil and violence. God chose him to build an ark to save his family and the animals from the great flood. He is regarded as the ancestor of all humanity after the flood and received the first covenant with the rainbow as a sign.

keyEvents.title: Noah finds favor with God
keyEvents.description: In a time when human wickedness was great on the earth, Noah found favor in the Lord's eyes because he was a righteous and blameless man who walked with God.

keyEvents.title: God's command to build the ark
keyEvents.description: God revealed to Noah that He would destroy the earth with a flood and gave him detailed instructions to build an ark of cypress wood to save his family and the animals.

keyEvents.title: Noah Enters the Ark and the Flood Comes
keyEvents.description: Noah entered the ark with his family and all the animals as God had commanded. Then God caused it to rain for forty days and forty nights, and the water covered the whole earth.

keyEvents.title: The Waters Recede and Noah Leaves the Ark
keyEvents.description: After the waters had receded, Noah sent out a dove that returned with an olive leaf. Finally, God opened the ark, and Noah could go out with his family and all the animals.

keyEvents.title: Noah's Sacrifice and God's Covenant with the Rainbow
keyEvents.description: Noah built an altar and offered sacrifices to the Lord. God established a covenant with Noah and promised never again to destroy the earth with a flood, setting the rainbow as a sign of this covenant.

keyEvents.title: Noah as a Model of Faith in the New Testament
keyEvents.description: The book of Hebrews highlights Noah as an example of faith, since he built the ark in reverence to save his household and became an heir of the righteousness that comes by faith. Peter also mentions Noah as a preacher of righteousness.
